panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Non-infra requests answered at the edge, per second — every route, and including requests rejected before a worker was chosen. Edge intake vs dispatched separates those two populations.

panels.title: Error ratio
panels.description: Share of non-infra edge requests whose outcome is error. Requests rejected before routing (404s, body-limit, backpressure) count here, so this is an edge error ratio rather than a worker one.

panels.title: P99 latency
panels.description: 99th percentile end-to-end request latency.

panels.title: Healthy workers
panels.description: Distinct workers whose circuit breaker admits requests. Every router replica exports the whole worker set with its own breaker state, so this takes the per-worker maximum first — a plain sum would report the fleet once per replica. A worker counts as healthy if any replica admits it; Worker health breaks the disagreement out per replica.

panels.title: Request rate by outcome
panels.description: success / error / cancelled.

panels.title: Request rate by mode
panels.description: prefill / decode / plain dispatch split.

panels.title: Request rate by cluster / namespace
panels.description: How the selected endpoint's traffic splits across the deployments serving it. Every other panel on this board is a rollup over that split; this is where an uneven or shifting split becomes visible without changing the variables.

panels.title: Request rate by worker
panels.description: Per-worker dispatch rate — reveals routing imbalance. Restricted to a non-empty worker_url so requests that never reached a worker do not appear here as an unlabelled series.

panels.title: Responses by HTTP status
panels.description: Client-visible HTTP status codes (2xx/4xx/5xx, 504=stale-cancel). Kubelet and scrape probes are excluded — the counter covers every route, and on a quiet deployment they are otherwise the only traffic shown.

panels.title: Response rate by route
panels.description: Response rate per HTTP route, excluding the health and discovery polling that would otherwise dominate every other route.

panels.title: Response code distribution
panels.description: Responses per status code as counts rather than a rate, stacked, so a short burst of one code stays legible next to steady-state traffic. Excludes probe routes, as above.

panels.title: Edge intake vs dispatched
panels.description: Chat-completions received at the HTTP edge against those that reached a worker. The gap is everything dropped before dispatch — backpressure rejections, early 4xx, client cancellations — which no per-worker panel can show. Dispatches are identified by a non-empty worker_url: the counter is written for every non-infra request and records an empty worker_url when nothing was dispatched. Deliberately unfiltered by model and worker, which are unknown at intake.

panels.title: Queued requests by replica
panels.description: Requests parked in the admission queue, per router replica. Sustained depth on one replica alone is a routing imbalance, not engine slowness.

panels.title: Admission wait quantiles
panels.description: Time spent parked in the admission queue before dispatch, among the requests that parked at all. Requests admitted straight through contribute no sample and do not pull the quantiles down, and requests that parked and were then shed contribute none either — so read this beside Queued requests, not as typical request delay. Whatever shows here is already lost to TTFT.

panels.title: Backpressure rejections
panels.description: Requests shed at admission because the queue was full, by model. These never reach a worker, so they are invisible to every per-worker panel.

panels.title: Request latency quantiles
panels.description: End-to-end request latency percentiles.

panels.title: TTFT quantiles (streaming)
panels.description: Time to first token (first upstream chunk) for streaming requests.

panels.title: Request latency distribution
panels.description: Latency histogram over time.

panels.title: ITL quantiles (streaming)
panels.description: Inter-token latency (gap between successive upstream chunks) for 2xx streaming requests. Bucket edges match the engine's sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds for direct quantile comparison.

panels.title: Stream outcomes (end-of-stream truth)
panels.description: End-of-stream classification for 2xx streaming responses: ok / inband_error / upstream_error / client_disconnect. inband_error is an engine that committed 200 OK then failed in-band — invisible to every headers-time metric.

panels.title: TTFT overhead share (router-attributable)
panels.description: Share of time-to-first-token the router itself accounts for (tokenize + admission wait + request build); the rest is engine prefill. Above 100% does not mean the router took longer than the whole request — the overhead histogram also samples 2xx streams that returned headers but no first token, which contribute no TTFT, so an excursion above 1 counts first-byteless streams rather than router slowness. Read a rising share below 1 as the router becoming the bottleneck; read a jump past 1 as streams dying before their first token.

panels.title: Workers by mode
panels.description: Registered worker count per mode.

panels.title: Worker health
panels.description: 1 = breaker admits requests, 0 = open.

panels.title: Circuit breaker state
panels.description: 0=closed, 1=open, 2=half_open.

panels.title: In-flight requests per worker
panels.description: Requests currently dispatched to each worker.

panels.title: Active load — prefill tokens
panels.description: Per-worker prefill-token load tracked by the active-load policy.

panels.title: Active load — decode blocks
panels.description: Per-worker decode-block load tracked by the active-load policy.

panels.title: Overlap blocks quantiles
panels.description: Cache-aware-zmq overlap-block count at policy selection.

panels.title: Cache-aware lookup health (all replicas)
panels.description: Traffic-weighted fleet lookup health, summed across router replicas and kept per model because ratios are not additive across models. Match is the matched/query block ratio among tree lookups; coverage is the fraction of policy evaluations that reached a tree lookup. Low match with a healthy tree points to a token/render/hash parity mismatch. Low coverage exposes early exits such as hash_config_unknown. Admission races can repeat evaluations, while parked hand-offs skip them, so neither series is request-level. Split to "Cache-aware lookup health by replica" only to test whether a single replica is responsible. Match (ceiling) is the best overlap ANY worker held; selected is what the worker actually picked held, and is the only one of the two comparable to the engine's sglang:cached_tokens_total / sglang:prompt_tokens_total. The gap between them is locality the load gate gave up; break it down with sgl_router_matched_overlap_blocks_total minus sgl_router_selected_overlap_blocks_total by decision. What remains below selected is cache state that changed between selection and prefill.

panels.title: Cache-aware routing decisions (all replicas)
panels.description: Fleet-wide terminal cache-aware routing decisions summed across router replicas, one outcome per policy evaluation rather than per request: admission races can evaluate repeatedly and parked hand-offs skip evaluation. Read this for the outcome mix and its trend; drop to "Cache-aware policy evaluations by replica" only to test whether a single replica is responsible. cache_hit falling while below_threshold, matched_workers_ineligible or cache_worker_queued rises is the signature of locality loss.

panels.title: Queue gate: prefix given up vs prefix available (p50 blocks)
panels.description: The queue gate is a binary test on num_waiting_reqs and ignores how much cached prefix a request would lose, so these two curves are how you tell whether that simplification is costing anything. Blue is the overlap of every cache-aware selection; orange is the overlap of just the ones the gate sent elsewhere (cache_worker_queued). Tracking together means the gate diverts a representative sample and the simple test is fine. Orange sitting materially above blue means it is trading large cached prefixes to dodge short queues — the signal to weigh forgone prefill against expected wait instead of thresholding on the queue alone, not to retune --worker-queue-limit.

panels.title: Locality loss by decision
panels.description: Blocks the best-matching worker held minus the blocks the worker actually selected held, over query blocks — the prefix locality each routing decision gave up. Zero means the decision cost nothing.

panels.title: Cache-aware lookup health by replica
panels.description: Per-replica lookup health; use "Cache-aware lookup health (all replicas)" for the fleet ratio. Match is the weighted matched/query block ratio among tree lookups; coverage is the fraction of policy evaluations that reached a tree lookup. Low match with a healthy tree points to a token/render/hash parity mismatch. Low coverage exposes early exits such as hash_config_unknown. Admission races can repeat evaluations, while parked hand-offs skip them, so neither series is request-level. Match (ceiling) is the best overlap ANY worker held; selected is what the worker actually picked held, and is the only one of the two comparable to the engine's sglang:cached_tokens_total / sglang:prompt_tokens_total. The gap between them is locality the load gate gave up; break it down with sgl_router_matched_overlap_blocks_total minus sgl_router_selected_overlap_blocks_total by decision. What remains below selected is cache state that changed between selection and prefill.

targets.expr: (sum by (instance, model_id) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{serving_endpoint=~"$endpoint",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",model_id=~"$model_id",decision=~"cache_hit|below_threshold|matched_node_unowned|matched_workers_ineligible|cache_worker_queued|cache_hit_all_queued"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (instance, model_id) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{serving_endpoint=~"$endpoint",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (instance, model_id) (rate(sgl_router_cache_aware_decisions_total{serving_endpoint=~"$endpoint",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",model_id=~"$model_id"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Cache-aware policy evaluations by replica
panels.description: Per-replica terminal policy-evaluation rate, not request rate: admission races can evaluate repeatedly and parked hand-offs skip evaluation. Series are unstacked so each decision reads its own rate off the axis; use "Cache-aware routing decisions (all replicas)" for the fleet-wide mix. below_threshold isolates tree/hash misses; load_imbalance is intentional; matched_node_unowned identifies tree lifecycle state; cache_worker_queued means every worker holding the prefix was over --worker-queue-limit and the request went elsewhere; cache_hit_all_queued means EVERY worker in the fleet was over it — the pick goes among queueing workers and under sampled min-load picks usually does NOT land on the cache home (saturation signal, not locality — alert on it); matched_workers_ineligible means the owners were not candidates at all (wrong pool, unhealthy, breaker open, or already at the router admission cap); hash_config_unknown and tokenization_unavailable identify routing-input failures. request_body_unavailable or request_json_invalid indicates a broken ingress invariant and emits an error log.

panels.title: KV tree nodes by replica
panels.description: A sharp per-replica drop exposes a cold router tree immediately. Compare with bootstrap state and below_threshold decisions.

panels.title: KV bootstrap settled by replica
panels.description: 0 while peer bootstrap is pending, 1 after it settles. Pair with tree nodes: settled=1 plus a tiny tree means bootstrap timed out or recovered incomplete state.

panels.title: KV fleet bimodal by replica
panels.description: 1 while the fleet carries both KV-block hashing modes, so every selection dual-hashes. Expected across a rolling update; a stuck 1 means some worker never finished the switch.

panels.title: KV bootstrap peers by replica
panels.description: Sibling router replicas visible to peer bootstrap. Zero on a fresh replica means it must rebuild its tree from live events alone.

panels.title: KV bootstrap rank outcomes
panels.description: Engine ranks by final bootstrap verdict. Counts ranks, not fetches — one accepted fetch can settle several ranks.

panels.title: KV peer snapshot fetch outcomes
panels.description: Peer snapshot fetches by outcome. Counts fetches, not ranks — a rank can outlive many rejected fetches.

panels.title: Sticky-session outcomes
panels.description: hit / assigned / remap / no_routing_key.

panels.title: Decode-affinity outcomes
panels.description: same_host_picked / fallback_breaker / fallback_load_imbalance.

panels.title: Stale-request cancellations
panels.description: Stale-request cancellations fired by the janitor.
